cases.description: Single-mapped kind='venue' crawl target. The posts repeatedly give the mapped venue's OWN street and number, spelled 'Tereza' where the catalogue spells 'Teresa' — one letter apart. The audit's textual check compares name and neighbourhood only, so it cannot see the street at all and flags the pair. Expected: a consensus confirm on matched_field=street that closes the flag.

canned_model_answer.reason: The posts give this venue's own street and number; Teresa/Tereza is a spelling difference, not a different street.

cases.description: The decisive arm-A-versus-arm-B case (plan §D). The CATALOGUED neighbourhood ('Parnamirim') is the erroneous field: it appears in none of the handle's own posts, which say 'Casa Forte'. A reviewer shown only name + neighbourhood returned a confident, unanimous and WRONG contradict 5/5 live; adding the street flips it to a unanimous, correctly-reasoned confirm citing the street. Expected: confirm on matched_field=street, never neighborhood.

canned_model_answer.reason: The post gives the same street and number as the catalogue venue despite spelling and neighbourhood-label differences.

cases.description: The structural-gate case (plan §F item 3). One handle, TWO mapped sibling venues in different neighbourhoods, sharing one pool of 12 'Amigos Park' posts that cannot belong to both. Asked independently per sibling, the live model returned confirm 10/10 for BOTH, one run even citing house number 30 for a venue catalogued at 50. Sampling cannot detect that. Expected: skipped_multi_mapped for both siblings, with ZERO model calls charged.
